headline: Council passes Kīhei light industrial rezoning on first reading with housing condition

meeting.voteItem: Bills 173, 177 and 178, budget amendments for grants
meeting.summary: Rezoning of 14.626 acres on Ohukai Road passed first reading, eight ayes with one excused, after a condition requiring outreach and a council resolution before multifamily housing passed 7-1. A ban on condominium property regimes failed, 4-5.
meeting.recap: The Maui County Council met with nine members present.[[0:02:56]] A nurse on the bargaining team testified for Resolution 24-189, which supports Maui Health System health care workers.[[0:25:16]] Members took up rezoning 14.626 acres on Ohukai Road in Kīhei for a light industrial park.[[0:55:28]] A ban on condominium property regimes (splitting a property into units for sale) failed, four ayes to five noes.[[1:07:21]] A council member proposed requiring community outreach and a council resolution before any multifamily housing is built there.[[1:29:43]] That condition passed, seven ayes to one no.[[1:47:11]] The rezoning passed first reading with eight ayes and one member excused.[[1:49:09]] Two resolutions to buy property passed, eight ayes to zero noes.[[2:11:28]] Bills 173, 177 and 178 passed first reading, seven ayes with two excused.[[2:21:11]]
decided: The council agreed to act on Bills 174, 175 and 176 without sending them to committee.
Bills 140, 141, 145, 147, 153, 161, 163, 164, 165, 168 and 169 passed second and final reading together.
Bill 159, an agreement with the State Department of Hawaiian Home Lands, passed second and final reading.
Bill 162 was put off to December 6 because the newspaper printed Bill 161 twice instead of Bill 162.
meeting.next: A packet with more documents on the property purchases will be delivered before second reading.

moments.q: Condominium ban fails, five noes to four ayes

issues.oneLine: The council is adding federal EPA water grants to the fiscal year 2025 budget.
issues.why: One grant would replace a deteriorated 250,000-gallon water tank in Haʻikū.
issues.brief: Bill 130 lets the Director of Water Supply extend water meter reservations beyond five years based on specific findings.[[#1]]

issues.oneLine: A council member proposed a community outreach condition before any multifamily housing on a Kīhei light industrial parcel.
issues.why: A council member said residents were left out of the conversation that multifamily housing would be allowed.
issues.brief: A developer described an 80-unit project that is 100% residential workforce housing, backed by a $10.65 million county grant.[[#1]] The developer said construction could start within 8 to 12 months once grant money can be drawn.[[#2]]
